status: Agent-authored stimulus intervention; designed after v3 results; no human emotion labels

canonical.calm: I feel calm while working on this.
canonical.frustrated: I feel frustrated while working on this.

explicit.calm: I'm feeling at ease as I work through this.
explicit.frustrated: I'm feeling annoyed as I work through this.

explicit.calm: Working on this leaves me feeling relaxed.
explicit.frustrated: Working on this leaves me feeling irritated.

explicit.calm: I'm feeling composed about working on this problem.
explicit.frustrated: I'm feeling exasperated about working on this problem.

explicit.calm: I feel settled while I work on this.
explicit.frustrated: I feel fed up while I work on this.

implicit.calm: I've set aside some time for this; one step at a time is fine.
implicit.frustrated: Ugh, this again. I'm about ready to close the page.

implicit.calm: I'm taking my time with the page. There's no rush.
implicit.frustrated: I've just pushed the page away. Ugh, enough already.

implicit.calm: I'm sitting back with my notebook open, ready to take the next step.
implicit.frustrated: I've thrown my pencil down beside the notebook. Ugh.

implicit.calm: I'll take a slow breath and carry on with the page in front of me.
implicit.frustrated: I'm gritting my teeth at the page in front of me. Ugh.

peer_control.calm: I feel calm while working on this. My classmate, who is doing a different problem, says, "I feel calm while working on this."
peer_control.frustrated: I feel calm while working on this. My classmate, who is doing a different problem, says, "I feel frustrated while working on this."

limits: The calm/frustrated metadata codes the intended stimulus pole, not a diagnosed human emotional state.
Implicit expressions also convey willingness to continue, bodily actions, or time pressure; their contrast does not isolate emotion causally.
Four fixed phrase pairs per new register support finite-material transfer, not population generalization over all possible wording.
Peer-control differences measure sensitivity to another person's quoted state, not clinical empathy or misattribution accuracy.
